children: selection for the U.S. Navy's F/A-XX fighter program adds another important pillar to its defense business, though the firm expects commercial aircraft trends to remain more relevant to the stock in the near term.

Analyst Kristine Liwag described the contract award as a positive surprise, especially after Boeing secured the Air Force's F-47 fighter program last year. Together, the two wins give Boeing a prime role in both major U.S. sixth-generation fighter efforts, Morgan Stanley said.

The bank expects the new program to strengthen Boeing's longer-term position in combat aircraft. The F/A-XX development phase is valued at more than $20 billion and is designed to replace the Navy's F/A-18 Super Hornet and EA-18G Growler fleets.

Morgan Stanley also cautioned that investors may seek greater clarity on the program's financial terms. Boeing has faced cost pressures on several fixed-price development contracts, making execution and contract economics important factors as the fighter program progresses.

The firm kept its Equal-weight rating and $250 price target on Boeing. Its valuation framework is based on 20 times projected 2028 free cash flow, reflecting an expectation that normalized cash generation could become a larger focus for investors.

title: Morgan Stanley Calls Boeing's Fighter Win a 'Major Strategic' Victory
